goal.startingPoint: Ten weeks off with a stress reaction in the left shin. My physio cleared me to start walk-run.

promptHead: Athlete goal: return to running since Mon Sep 7 2026, 1 week in; the athlete says: Ten weeks off with a stress reaction in the left shin. My physio cleared me to start walk-run.

new.headline: Your first week back went cleanly: three walk-runs, all at 0/10 pain and an easy effort. Next week repeats that session twice, then takes one small step on Saturday with longer running stretches.

flags.title: Shin the morning after
flags.detail: Check the shin each morning after a run. This was pain-free week 1 of 4, and any pain, even pain that settles, restarts the count.

flags.title: Saturday's longer running stretches
flags.detail: This is your first time running 1 min 30 s without a break. Keep it as easy as last week, and stop and walk home if the shin aches.

flags.title: Keep the running gentle
flags.detail: Last week's running felt like effort 3/10, with heart rate around 122. Keep it there even as you feel stronger, because the shin sets the limit, not your fitness.

flags.title: Mid-October goal
flags.detail: Running 30 minutes without walking by mid-October would mean building faster than is safe for your shin. Plan on a later date.

new.analysis:
**Your first week back went exactly as it should.** All three walk-runs stayed at 0/10 pain, and the shin was quiet. Every session felt like effort 3/10, so this counts as the first of the four pain-free weeks you need before any harder running.

**Your splits show 5 rounds of 1 minute running and 2 minutes walking each time.** That is 5 minutes of running per session and 15 minutes for the week. Your heart rate averaged about 122 and never went above 130, so your heart and lungs are well ahead of the work.

**The shin sets how fast you build, not your fitness.** Bone gets used to running more slowly than muscle or breathing does. So your running minutes go up by about 10 percent a week, which takes you from 15 minutes to 16 next week.

**Repeating Monday and Wednesday is deliberate.** Two sessions you already know are safe give the shin a calm start to the week. If Saturday stirs anything up, you will know exactly what caused it.

**Your physio's stop rule comes first.** If the shin aches during a run, stop and walk home, then note how it feels the next morning. If it is worse the next morning, the next step gets smaller, not bigger.

**Mid-October is too soon for 30 minutes without walking.** At about 10 percent a week, you will be running around 8 minutes per session by mid-October. Thirty minutes nonstop is about six times your current running, so it is more likely a winter goal.

**Feeling nervous is normal after ten weeks off.** The plan keeps each step so small that it should feel almost too easy. Keep doing both physio sessions each week, as you did last week, because they help the shin cope with running.

settingsProposalBullets: You restarted with walk-runs of 5 rounds of 1 minute running and 2 minutes walking, three times a week.
Move your goal of running 30 minutes without walking from mid-October to a later date you agree with your physio.

safetyCallouts.title: Call your physio if the shin hurts.
safetyCallouts.body: If you feel pain in one spot on the shin, pain when walking, or pain that is worse the next morning, stop running and check with your physio before your next session.
